report:
T6 is implemented on task/T6. HEAD is 3e1d450 and is pushed: local and origin/task/T6 have the same hash. The base is T5 at 31f470f. When I started, the worktree had no T6 commits and no uncommitted changes, so I began from T5's committed state.

What now happens when the split check fails
- New `src/+mwecmass/+realise/+modular_precast/solve.m` is called from `solve_and_extract.m`. It runs only when the split check fails and a ballast module k* exists.
- Solver variables are z_ballast, t_k*, the t_i of the hollow modules above k*, and vs in the last step. fmincon uses 'sqp' with ConstraintTolerance 1e-6 (TOL_EQ). The variables are scaled to their bound box and clamped back inside the bounds.
- Objective: the sum of squared relative deviations of CG_total(3), coupled T_heave and coupled T_pitch. Equalities: flotation M/(rho_w V_sub) - 1 and GM/GM2 - 1, both taken from F10.
- Each step has two phases:
  - Phase 1 minimises the squared GM residual with flotation as its equality. If GM cannot be reached, the step still ends on a design that floats, and the draft is released only when flotation itself fails (AGENTS 3 items 31 and 32).
  - Phase 2 minimises the objective with both equalities, starting from a phase-1 point that meets both.
- The step keeps the best design it evaluated, ranked: both equalities held (lowest objective first), then flotation held (smallest |GM residual|), then neither.
- Escalation:
  - fixed_draft runs first.
  - spill runs only when the two equalities are not both met and module k*+1 exists and is hollow. It uses the same ballast variable with the upper bound raised to e(k*+2). Modules wholly below z_ballast get t = NaN.
  - draft_free runs only when flotation is still not met.
  - The escalation stops as soon as the check passes (accepted) or both equalities hold (that step's optimum is the closest fail).
  - Otherwise the closest fail is the best-ranked design evaluated in any step, rebuilt on its adaptive fit.
- Failed evaluations: VoidClosed, JointNotNested, FitNotConverged and non-finite solver points return Inf and are counted and noted. If fmincon then errors, the step keeps its best point. Any other error raised during an evaluation is rethrown.
- Inner surfaces keep their knot vectors during a solve (knots_from). A step restarts when the adaptive fit at its point has a different knot structure, as in contract §7 item 4.
- F7 is called once per vs and cached. Evaluated points are cached under an exact key.
- S8 `solver` holds one entry per step (split, fixed_draft, spill, draft_free); `escalation` is the last step run.
- `stage3_report.m` replaces print_realised. It prints the modules, each metric (value, Stage-2 value, deviation, limit, pass), both equality residuals (GM marked as not part of the check), the steps and the notes. `reason` lists the failing metrics, the escalation notes and which closest-fail rule applied.

Orchestrator decisions
1. t_max,i = d_close([e(i), e(i+1)]) - eps_fit/2 for k* and every hollow module. The T5 shell root search now uses it too.
2. `realise_modules` asks for an inner set over the whole hollow range while t < t_max_hollow; above that it asks only for the span of the modules that use that t, and reuses a set only if its range covers that span (`ctx.set_ranges`). This departs from contract §7 item 2 (one set per t over the whole hollow range) only when t exceeds the hollow-range bound.
3. Kernel errors count as failed evaluations.

I added two options to `solve_and_extract`: `opts.d_close_fn` (to set t_max in tests) and `opts.escalate` (false keeps only the split). The inner-set provider now takes a third argument, z_range.

Tests: every result in the next section comes from the stand-in kernel (SK). There was no whole-pipeline or C1 run, and MWEC_REGRESSION was never set.
- `test_precast_stage3_solve` (box and cylinder) asserts, by construction: escalation order; the condition that starts each step (spill and draft only after failed equalities); the draft kept unless draft_free ran; variable bounds; modules below z_ballast solid; props and final_props taken from the stored body; stored objective and violation equal to those recomputed from the stored props; status equals check.pass; volume closure.
- Cases S and D first prove from computed mass bounds that flotation is out of reach (S inside k*, D at the Stage-2 draft for every design), then assert that spill (S) and the draft release (D) ran.
- Case G is the forced-infeasible case (GM2 = 100 m) on the cylinder through F14 `run.m`. It asserts the failed status, the GM failure, the closest-fail reason and that final_props is the stored realised design, not Stage 2. Figures and STEP are switched off in tests, as contract §3 requires.

Tests run
- `octave --no-gui --quiet /home/user/wt/T6/tests/run_tests.m`: 32 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (regression), 1045.2 s.
- `test_precast_stage3_solve` (658.9 s):
  - C: split > fixed_draft. Flotation residual 1.16e-08, GM residual 6.13e-08, T_pitch deviation 0.1212, so it is stored as the fixed-draft closest fail.
  - S: heaviest design inside k* is 6872.731 kg against 7687.500 kg displaced. Steps split > fixed_draft > spill. Flotation residual 1.6e-08, GM residual 1.27. The draft was not released; closest fail.
  - D: lightest design is 4805.495 kg against 307.500 kg displaced. Steps run up to draft_free. vs -0.5 m against 2.4 m at Stage 2, flotation residual 0.291.
  - G: steps split > fixed_draft > spill. Flotation residual 7.85e-08, GM residual -0.997, status failed.
- `test_precast_solve_failed_evals` (22.0 s): the steps run are fixed_draft and draft_free, with the spill-not-possible note, failed evaluations noted, and the stored t = 100 mm, the only thickness the test provider can fit adaptively. It runs on a hand-made start design and calls solve directly, so the split does not run.
- `test_precast_inner_ranges` (3.2 s): requested ranges [0.1 -2.5 0.5; 0.3 -0.5 0.5], then [0.3 -1.5 0.5]; a kept set is reused only when it covers the span.
- `test_precast_stage3` (T5, now split-only, 164.7 s): passes.

What this does not show
- Octave's sqp is weak on this problem. It warns that the QP subproblem is non-convex or infeasible, and its sqp.m crashes on empty multipliers (line 482).
- In C, Octave reached both equalities but did not bring T_pitch within 10 %. In D it ended on a fully submerged design with flotation residual 0.291, although some design between M_min and the fully submerged displaced mass should float. Whether MATLAB fmincon converges in these cases is unchecked here; the J2 runs (owner checkpoint) will show it.
- The test assertions are structural. Solver quality is printed, not gated.

open_issues: Octave 8.4 sqp (behind the test shim) converges poorly here: it warns that the QP subproblem is non-convex, unbounded or infeasible, and it crashes at sqp.m line 482 when qp returns empty multipliers. Stage 3 treats these errors as a solver stop and keeps the step's best point. Consequences in the tests: C stays at T_pitch dev 0.1212 after reaching both equalities, and D ends fully submerged (vs = -0.5) with flotation residual 0.291 although some design between M_min and the fully submerged displaced mass should float. MATLAB fmincon is the target and should be checked on the J2 C1 runs

Test-shim fix outside my task's file list: tests/octave_shims/fmincon.m now returns empty multipliers instead of erroring when sqp returns a 0x0 lambda after a failed QP. The edit adds 6 lines with a doc line. The ownership map does not list the shims; the orchestrator should confirm the edit is acceptable

Contract section 7 item 2 deviation: an inner set whose t is at or above d_close(hollow range) - eps_fit/2 is fitted over the span of its modules, not the whole hollow range. Orchestrator decision 1 requires this, but the contract text should be updated

Closest fail when no step meets both equalities: the candidates are every evaluated point, including finite-difference neighbours and adaptive rebuilds, because fmincon iterates are not exposed portably (Octave's OutputFcn gives only init/done). Candidates are ranked flotation-first (both equalities held, then flotation held, then neither) per AGENTS 3 item 32. This is my reading of 'iterate with the smallest equality violation'; confirm with the owner
New production test hooks in solve_and_extract: opts.escalate (false = split only) and opts.d_close_fn; the inner_fn provider now takes a z_range argument
test_precast_stage3_solve takes about 11 min and the full suite about 17.5 min in Octave, because each stand-in build_body takes about 1.5 s per evaluation
